parsed.explanation: A trans-specific criminalisation statute ('identifying as transgender,' up to 3 years; longer for advocacy; a duty to report) has passed parliament in May 2026 and awaits a president widely expected to assent — the supreme court deferred review until signature, so no remedy exists yet. Even without assent, the documented baseline is severe: 'unnatural carnal knowledge' (3 years), documented mob justice with impunity, no anti-discrimination protection, and state security raiding and closing the only LGBT office in the capital. Recourse is absent (community groups secret/online; oversight findings show closure, not relief). Prison-placement rules are undocumented, so imprisonment carries unmitigated birth-sex custody risk. The visitor-facing statute is a known universal exposure if outed; whether it reaches short-term visitors is an open question, which carries little weight either way. Extrapolating from the criminalisation regime, state-adjacent hostility and absent protection, this sits in the High Risk band, above active-enforcement profiles only because enforcement of the new offence is not yet recorded.
